Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
Council Meeting of April 27, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.
  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5
  minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from
  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it
  is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission.
  Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.
  l  Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed
  below for the respective City Council Dates:
  ¡  April 20, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡  April 27, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting;
however, members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access
options 1 and 2 noted above.

Inglewood, California
  April 27, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California, held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, April 27, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.

  Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a

  Parking Authority Chairman /Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*

  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  and Joint Powers Authority.

  Yakema Decatur, Deputy to the City Manager/Housing Protection Deputy Director,
  presented the Staff Report.

  Mayor Butts inquired about the impact of the Ordinance on Section 8 tenants.

  Yakema informed Mayor Butts that they are protected from evictions but not the rent
  increase regulations.

  Mayor Butts also inquired if the owners of properties with 5 or more units, who have
  kept their rents very low and less than median, are allowed an additional Consumer
  Price Index (CPI) percentage in addition to the current 5%?

  Yakema stated they are not, but she wouldn’t be opposed to it.

  Mayor Butts suggested to the Council that the current rent increase for properties of 5
  units or more is capped at 3%; however, he stated that the properties whose rents are less
  than 80% of Fair Market Value should be eligible for 5% plus CPI (upon approval).

  Yakema requested that the City Council also consider amending the proposed Ordinance
  to provide an additional rent increase percentage for Mom and Pop Owners who have
  kept their rents low as well.

  Council Member Morales commented and asked for the definition of Mom and Pop
  owners.

  Yakema commented and Mom and Pop Owners have four units or less. She also stated
  the proposed Ordinance is bringing four or less units under the City’s jurisdiction. She
  stated that they would still get the same rent increases that State law currently allows.

  Council Member Morales agreed and asked how the process would go to receive an
  additional 2%?

  Yakema stated the property owners email her and provide her with the number of
  bedrooms, the current rent, and the last time the rent was raised. She would approve the
  increase if the rent were raised less than 12 months and the current rent is less than 80%
  of Fair Market Value.

  Council Member Morales suggested leaving the process as Ms. Yakema Decatur stated
  and recommended a friendly amendment of the 2% be added.

  Mayor Butts suggested making another amendment to the “just cause” evictions that are
  listed in the Ordinance. He clarified that the City does not have a “just cause” eviction
  for renovations but substantial renovations of varying amounts; the owners can recoup
  through rent at a cap rate of 50%.

  Yakema Decatur clarified the current Ordinance lists substantial renovations as a “just
  cause” for an eviction, which she feels would be used as a loophole because of the
  uncertain definition of substantial remodeling.

  5
  April 27, 2021

Mayor  Butts recommended  the  removal  of  “just  cause”  evictions  for  substantial
  renovations.

Yakema  Decatur stated the proposed Ordinance combines substantial remodels with
  capital improvements. Instead of it being fees where owners could recoup 50% of their
  costs, it would be considered rent which would protect the owner if the tenant chooses
  not to pay.

  Mayor Butts stated due to COVID and the problems property owners had with collecting
  rent, he recommended another amendment of commencing the Housing Protection
  Residential Registration in January 2022, instead of October 2021.

  Yakema Decatur agreed and asked if the Council would come up with a time frame in
  which owners would register, and if owners fail to register, they would be required to
  pay registration fees that could not be passed down to the tenant. She also stated that it
  is uncertain how the pandemic would impact courts because of the State Legislation, and
  it gives the City time to see how it would affect the constituents of Inglewood. She
  believed courts would be bombarded with evictions if the State does not extend the
  eviction protection order.

  Mayor Butts asked what the penalty was if owners don’t register by the deadline?

  Yakema Decatur informed Mayor Butts that the owners would have to pay the
  registration fee after 90 days.

  Council Member Morales reiterated that owners should take advantage of the benefits of
  registering before the deadline.

  Mayor Butts stated that if property owners register their properties by January 7, 2022,
  they would not be charged enrollment fees for the program until October 1, 2022. The
  opposite will be true if owners do not register by January 7, 2022; registration fees
  would be assessed. After speaking with Yakema Decatur, Mayor Butts made a motion
  for the registration period to commence on January 8, 2022, through March 31, 2022.

  Yakema Decatur reiterated that if owners do not register by the end of March, they
  would be required to begin paying fees in April; if payments are not paid then, penalties
  start in May 2022. Ms. Decatur further stated that Section 8 tenants makes up part of the
  city’s rental population, and advocated that the proposed laws should apply to them as
  well. She stated that Section 8 tenants should be treated with the same respect and have
  the same rights as non-Section eight tenants. She stated that there shouldn’t be a
  difference made between the two because it seems discriminatory. She commented that
  if a unit is occupied by a Section 8 tenant, regardless of the amount the tenant is paying
  out of pocket, the owner gets the full rent. She concluded by saying that the City’s rent
  regulations and eviction protections should be based on property type not based on the
  tenant.

  Mayor Butts recommended a motion be made to amend the proposed Ordinance, which
  affords Section 8 tenants the same protections as non-Section eight tenants, which will
  be determined by the property type and not the occupant.

  After further discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to
  Ordinance No. 21-08 to allow, upon approval, rent increases of 5% plus CPI for
  properties of 5 or more units whose rents are less than 80% of Fair Market Value, and
  allow, upon approval, an additional rent increase of 2% (not to exceed 10%) for
  properties of 4 or less units whose rents are less than 80% of Fair Market Value. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
